paragraphs.text: Heb., Said. He slighted not the divine oracle nor his father’s charge; but was still plodding and talking of it to himself till it was done.
See 1Ki 5:3, and compare this chapter with that: the one giveth light to the other; as glasses set one against another do cast a mutual light.
paragraphs.anchor: To build a house for the name of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: David had built a fair palace: but Solomon’s far exceeded it: this was a house for his kingdom. Our William Rufus found much fault with Westminster Hall for being built too small: and took a plot for one far more spacious to be added unto it. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And a house for his kingdom.

By this thankful acknowledgment he seeketh to ingratiate. Gratiarum actio est ad plus dandum invitatio.
paragraphs.anchor: As thou didst deal with David my father.

paragraphs.text: Not to be impiae gentis arcanum, as Florus basely slandereth this temple.
Excellently great, as he afterwards saith. {2Ch 2:9}
paragraphs.anchor: And the house which I build is great.

paragraphs.text: And must therefore be served like himself.
Whether deputed, as princes, or reputed, as idols.

He is ανεπιγραπτος incomprehensible, incircumscriptible: good without quality, great without quantity, everlasting without time, present everywhere without place, containing all things without extent: he filleth all places without compression or straitening of another, or the contraction, extension, condensation, or rarefaction of himself: he is within all things, and contained of nothing: without all things, and sustained of nothing.
paragraphs.anchor: Seeing the heavens and heaven of heavens.
Send me now therefore a man.

paragraphs.anchor: My servants shall be with thy servants.

paragraphs.text: Yet was it not so great as the temple at Ephesus, but far more wonderful. See on 2Ch 2:5.

And shall not Christ’s servants and ministers have due maintenance? That which is given to them is given to Christ; as that which is here promised to Hiram’s servants, is promised to Hiram’s self, {1Ki 5:6; 1Ki 5:11} who, if he did not like it, is promised more. {1Ki 5:6} The difference of the food and measures given by Solomon here, over and above that in 1Ki 5:11, may stand in this, that the former was for king Hiram’s court and household: and this here, for his workmen in Lebanon.
paragraphs.anchor: And, behold, I will give to thy servants.

paragraphs.text: It is a great mercy of God to any people, that they have good governors; and the contrary. {Isa 3:2-4}
paragraphs.anchor: Because the Lord hath loved his people.

paragraphs.text: Egregia est confessio. Aristotle held the world’s eternity.
paragraphs.anchor: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, that made heaven and earth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., His servant and architect. The Vulgate hath it, Hiram my father, i.e., one whom, for his virtue, wisdom, and industry, I honour as a father.

Some men are good at anything; as Hippias, called Omniseius by Apuleius. {a} He was not only a general scholar, but made with his own hands he ring he wore, the clothes he had on, the shoes on his feet, &c., as Cicero {b} tells us.
{a} Apulei. Florid.
{b} De Orator, lib. iii.

See the benefit of a good neighbour, ready to every good office, as Hesiod describeth him.
See 1Ch 22:2.
Hereby were shadowed out the several offices in Christ’s Church: this St Paul setteth forth by the similitude of the diffferent members in man’s body, &c.
